name: Halverson Synth-Wool Single-Breasted Suit
description:
A reliable mid-tier two-piece suit in a dark charcoal or slate blue synth-wool blend, constructed with real stitched interfacing and a full canvas chest piece — an uncommon feature at this price point. Halverson & Crane have been producing this cut for thirty years with minimal changes, and that consistency is part of the appeal. The lapels are moderate, the trousers are cut straight with a slight taper, and the lining is a clean gunmetal grey that holds its shape through daily wear. It's not trying to be remarkable.

This is the suit a Tier 2 supervisor wears to quarterly reviews, a Tier 3 mid-level administrator keeps at the office for unexpected client meetings, and a Tier 2 union rep puts on when testifying before a municipal arbitration board. Augment-compatible back panel is available as a Φ15 alteration option from most Halverson retail kiosks. No geneware accommodation in the standard cut, but the trousers have modest waistband flex.
cultural_context: The Halverson suit is the suit of aspiration and maintenance — worn by people who are either climbing toward something or working to hold on to what they have. It signals competence and effort without signaling wealth, which in certain Tier 3 environments is exactly right. A Tier 4 person wearing one reads as deliberately understated or as someone whose fortunes recently changed.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 union organizer has worn the same Halverson suit to every negotiation for six years — a deliberate choice to never appear to have profited from the work.
The augment-compatible back panel alteration leaves a small rectangular seam that a Tier 4 interviewer clocks immediately, filing away a data point about the candidate's economic history.
Someone finds a Halverson suit in their deceased parent's closet, still in the dry-clean bag, never worn — purchased for an occasion that never came.
